schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
schemes.description: A central sector scheme launched in February 2019 to supplement the financial needs of cultivable land-holding farmer families through direct income support.
schemes.benefits: Financial benefit of Rs 6,000 per year, transferred in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each, directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
schemes.eligibility: Landholding farmer families with cultivable land registered in their name as per state land records. Excluded categories include institutional landholders, present and former holders of constitutional posts, Ministers, MPs, MLAs, Mayors, and chairpersons of local bodies, serving or retired government employees and officers of Central/State Government departments, PSUs and autonomous bodies (except Class IV/Group D staff), pensioners receiving a monthly pension of Rs 10,000 or more, and individuals who paid income tax in the previous assessment year.
schemes.required_documents: Aadhaar card, land ownership/land records documents, and bank account details for Aadhaar-seeded DBT.
schemes.application_process: Register via the 'Farmers Corner' on the official PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in), or through the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Applicants can check eligibility and payment status using the 'Know Your Status' feature on the portal.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Cultivable land-holding farmer families across India.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY-Urban 2.0)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
schemes.description: The Government of India's flagship affordable housing scheme aimed at providing all-weather pucca houses to all eligible urban households, implemented through four verticals: Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH), and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).
schemes.benefits: Under BLC and AHP, financial assistance of up to Rs 2.5 lakh for EWS households (annual income up to Rs 3 lakh) to construct or purchase a pucca house. Under the Interest Subsidy Scheme, eligible EWS/LIG/MIG households (annual income up to Rs 3 lakh, Rs 6 lakh, and Rs 9 lakh respectively) receive an interest subsidy on home loans sanctioned and disbursed on or after 01.09.2024.
schemes.eligibility: The beneficiary family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India and must not have previously availed central or state government housing assistance or any PMAY-CLSS subsidy. Income limits vary by vertical and category (EWS: up to Rs 3 lakh/year; LIG: up to Rs 6 lakh/year; MIG: up to Rs 9 lakh/year for the Interest Subsidy Scheme). Eligibility is subject to verification by the respective States/UTs/ULBs/Central Nodal Agencies/Primary Lending Institutions.
schemes.required_documents: Proof of income for the respective category, and other documents as required for the chosen vertical (application/citizen assessment form). Specific document list is finalized during the verification process by the implementing agency.
schemes.application_process: Apply online through the official PMAY-Urban portal (pmaymis.gov.in) via the 'Citizen Assessment' section, selecting the appropriate vertical (BLC, AHP, ARH, or ISS). Once a vertical is selected it cannot be changed later. Filling the application form does not guarantee benefit; eligibility must be verified by the respective State/UT/ULB/CNA/PLI.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Economically Weaker Section (EWS), Low Income Group (LIG), and Middle Income Group (MIG) urban households without a pucca house.

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (implemented by the National Health Authority)
schemes.description: The world's largest publicly funded health insurance scheme, designed to provide free access to secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation for economically vulnerable families as part of the Ayushman Bharat initiative.
schemes.benefits: Health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation at empanelled public and private hospitals across India, on a cashless and paperless basis.
schemes.eligibility: Targets poor and vulnerable families identified based on deprivation and occupational criteria, covering approximately the bottom 40% of the population. Eligibility can be checked using the 'Am I Eligible' tool on the official PM-JAY website or app using mobile number and other details.
schemes.required_documents: Aadhaar card and other identity/eligibility verification documents as specified during the 'Am I Eligible' check; an Ayushman card is issued upon confirmation of eligibility.
schemes.application_process: Check eligibility via the 'Am I Eligible' tool on the official PM-JAY website (pmjay.gov.in) or the PM-JAY mobile app by entering mobile number and state details. Eligible beneficiaries receive an Ayushman Bharat card usable at empanelled hospitals.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Poor and vulnerable families identified through deprivation and occupational criteria.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY 2.0)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
schemes.description: A scheme launched on 1 May 2016 to provide deposit-free LPG connections to women from poor households, aiming to replace traditional cooking fuels with clean cooking gas.
schemes.benefits: Cash assistance of Rs 2,050 for a 14.2 kg cylinder connection (or Rs 1,300 for a 5 kg cylinder), covering the security deposit of the cylinder, pressure regulator, LPG hose, domestic gas consumer card, and inspection/installation/demonstration charges. All PMUY beneficiaries also receive their first LPG refill and a stove (hotplate) free of cost.
schemes.eligibility: The applicant must be a woman who has attained 18 years of age, there must be no other LPG connection from any Oil Marketing Company within the same household, and the adult woman must belong to a poor household based on submission of a deprivation declaration in the prescribed format.
schemes.required_documents: KYC application form, proof of identity (Aadhaar copy of applicant), proof of address (only if different from Aadhaar address, via self-declaration for migrants), ration card or other state government document certifying family composition, Aadhaar copies of the applicant and adult family members listed in that document, bank account details (passbook copy or cancelled cheque), and a Deprivation Declaration.
schemes.application_process: Apply online via the official PMUY portal (pmuy.gov.in) by selecting an Oil Marketing Company (Indane, Bharat Gas, or HP Gas) and completing the Ujjwala 2.0 connection form, or apply offline through the nearest LPG distributor using the KYC form.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Adult women from poor households without an existing LPG connection.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services
schemes.description: A National Mission for Financial Inclusion launched in August 2014 to ensure access to financial services such as banking, savings and deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension in an affordable manner.
schemes.benefits: A Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) account with no minimum balance requirement, a free RuPay debit card with in-built accident insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh, access to an overdraft facility of up to Rs 10,000 (subject to eligibility conditions), and easy access to banking services in rural areas through Bank Mitras.
schemes.eligibility: Not specified in the verified source beyond the account being opened for persons not already having a basic savings bank deposit account, at any bank branch or Business Correspondent (Bank Mitra) outlet.
schemes.required_documents: Not specified in the verified source; standard bank KYC documentation is required to open the account.
schemes.application_process: Open a Basic Savings Bank Deposit account at any bank branch or Business Correspondent (Bank Mitra) outlet, or via the application form available on the official PMJDY website (pmjdy.gov.in).
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Unbanked adults across India, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance (implemented via MUDRA Ltd., a subsidiary of SIDBI)
schemes.description: A flagship scheme launched on 8 April 2015 to provide collateral-free loans to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises for income-generating activities in manufacturing, trading, services, and allied agricultural activities.
schemes.benefits: Collateral-free loans up to Rs 20 lakh, classified into four categories based on business growth stage: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh), and Tarun Plus (above Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 20 lakh, for entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid a previous Tarun loan).
schemes.eligibility: Individuals, proprietary concerns, partnership firms, private limited companies, public companies, and other legal entities engaged in non-farm income-generating activities in manufacturing, trading, or services (or allied agricultural activities) with credit requirements up to Rs 20 lakh. The applicant should not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution and should have a satisfactory credit track record.
schemes.required_documents: Not specified in the verified source in full detail; general requirements include identity proof, address proof, and business-related documents as prescribed by the lending institution.
schemes.application_process: Apply through any Member Lending Institution (Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Small Finance Banks, NBFCs, or MFIs), selecting the appropriate loan category (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun, or Tarun Plus), or apply online through the Udyamimitra portal (udyamimitra.in) or MUDRA's official website (mudra.org.in).
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises and entrepreneurs, including women entrepreneurs.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation)
schemes.description: The flagship skill certification scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, enabling Indian youth to undertake industry-relevant skill training to secure a better livelihood, including through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL).
schemes.benefits: Free industry-relevant skill training and assessment, along with certification recognized across India. Not specified in the verified source: exact monetary incentive amounts, as these vary by scheme version and should be confirmed on the official portal.
schemes.eligibility: Candidates aged between 15 and 45 years, possessing an Aadhaar card and an Aadhaar-linked bank account, and fulfilling any additional criteria for the respective job role as defined by the awarding body.
schemes.required_documents: Aadhaar card and an Aadhaar-linked bank account. Additional documents may be required depending on the specific job role or training centre.
schemes.application_process: Register through the official PMKVY portal or the Skill India Digital Hub, locate a training centre by state, district, sector, and job role, and enrol for the desired course.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Indian youth, including school/college dropouts and unemployed individuals, seeking skill training and certification.

schemes.name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education
schemes.description: A 100% centrally funded merit-cum-means scholarship scheme launched in 2008 to provide financial assistance to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to pursue higher education.
schemes.benefits: Financial assistance disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer for the duration of the course, at rates specified in the official scheme guidelines. Not specified in the verified source: current exact scholarship amount, as it is subject to periodic revision and should be confirmed on the National Scholarship Portal.
schemes.eligibility: The applicant must be above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in the relevant stream from their Board of Examination in Class 12 (10+2 pattern) or equivalent, must be enrolled in a regular degree course (not correspondence, distance mode, or diploma), must be pursuing courses at institutions recognized by AICTE or the respective regulatory body, and must not be availing any other scholarship scheme including state-run scholarships or fee waivers.
schemes.required_documents: Class 12 marksheet, income certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), disability certificate (if applicable), Aadhaar card or an accepted alternate ID proof, and bank account details in the student's name.
schemes.application_process: Apply online exclusively through the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) by registering, filling in the application form, and uploading the required documents for institute and state-level verification.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Meritorious students from economically weaker sections pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies.

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs (implemented via India Post and authorized banks)
schemes.category: Savings and Financial Inclusion for the Girl Child
schemes.description: A government-backed small savings scheme launched on 22 January 2015 under the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign, designed to help parents or guardians build a financial corpus for a girl child's future education and marriage expenses.
schemes.benefits: A savings account offering a government-notified interest rate (reviewed quarterly; 8.2% per annum for the April-June 2026 quarter), compounded annually. Deposits qualify for tax deduction, and interest earned and maturity proceeds are tax-exempt, subject to conditions under the applicable tax provisions. Minimum annual deposit of Rs 250 and maximum of Rs 1.5 lakh. The account matures 21 years from the date of opening.
schemes.eligibility: The account can be opened by a parent or legal guardian for a girl child who is a citizen of India, from birth until she attains 10 years of age. A maximum of two accounts can generally be opened per family (with exceptions for twins/triplets, subject to documentary proof).
schemes.required_documents: Birth certificate of the girl child, identity and address proof of the parent/guardian, and other KYC documents as prescribed under the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme, 2019.
schemes.application_process: Open the account at any India Post office or a branch of an authorized commercial bank by submitting the prescribed application form along with required documents.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Parents or legal guardians of a girl child below the age of 10 years.

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
schemes.description: A central sector micro-credit scheme launched on 1 June 2020 to provide collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors, helping them restart or expand their businesses.
schemes.benefits: Collateral-free working capital loan starting at Rs 10,000 for the first cycle, with higher amounts of Rs 20,000 and Rs 50,000 available in subsequent cycles upon timely repayment. Beneficiaries also receive a 7% interest subsidy and cashback incentives of up to Rs 100 per month for adopting digital transactions.
schemes.eligibility: Street vendors possessing a valid Certificate of Vending or Identity Card issued by an Urban Local Body, or vendors identified in official surveys who have not yet received a Certificate of Vending or Identity Card, or vendors with a Letter of Recommendation from an Urban Local Body or Town Vending Committee.
schemes.required_documents: Aadhaar card, bank account details, and Certificate of Vending/Identity Card or Letter of Recommendation from the Urban Local Body/Town Vending Committee; a Survey Reference Number (SRN) is required for the online application.
schemes.application_process: Apply online through the official PM SVANidhi portal (pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in) using a mobile number linked to Aadhaar, selecting the vendor category and entering the Survey Reference Number, or apply offline with the help of a Banking Correspondent, Common Service Centre, or Urban Local Body.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services (implemented via SIDBI)
schemes.description: A scheme launched on 5 April 2016 to facilitate bank loans to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, and women entrepreneurs for setting up new (greenfield) enterprises in manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or the trading sector.
schemes.benefits: A composite loan (inclusive of term loan and working capital) between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore, covering up to 75-85% of the project cost depending on conditions. The interest rate is the lowest applicable rate of the bank for that category, not exceeding the base rate (MCLR) plus 3% plus tenure premium. The loan is repayable over 7 years with a maximum moratorium period of 18 months.
schemes.eligibility: The borrower must be a Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and/or woman entrepreneur above 18 years of age, setting up a greenfield (first-time) enterprise. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneur. The borrower must not be in default to any bank or financial institution.
schemes.required_documents: Caste/category certificate for SC/ST applicants, and supporting business documents such as equipment quotations, rental agreements, or purchase invoices. For non-individual entities, partnership deeds or Memorandum/Articles of Association must be provided.
schemes.application_process: Apply through the official Stand-Up India portal (standupmitra.in) by registering and answering the prompted questions, or approach a bank branch directly, or contact the Lead District Manager (LDM).
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, and women entrepreneurs setting up new enterprises.

schemes.name: ADIP Scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
schemes.description: A scheme in operation since 1981 to assist needy persons with disabilities in procuring durable, modern, standard aids and appliances that promote physical, social, and psychological rehabilitation by reducing the effects of disability and enhancing economic potential.
schemes.benefits: Financial assistance (grant-in-aid released through implementing agencies) toward the cost of assistive devices and aids/appliances, including essential surgical correction or intervention prior to fitment where required, subject to income ceiling conditions specified in the scheme guidelines.
schemes.eligibility: The beneficiary must be an Indian citizen of any age, possess an Aadhaar card and UDID/enrolment number, hold a Benchmark Disability Certificate (40% disability or more), and have a monthly income from all sources not exceeding Rs 30,000.
schemes.required_documents: Aadhaar card, UDID/enrolment number of the person with disability, Benchmark Disability Certificate, and income certificate (income certificate for beneficiaries in orphanages/half-way homes may be certified by the District Collector or head of the organization).
schemes.application_process: Register as a beneficiary online through the official ADIP portal (adip.depwd.gov.in) or through an approved implementing agency, such as recognized societies, charitable trusts, or National/Apex institutes functioning under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Persons with disabilities (Divyangjan) meeting the specified disability and income criteria.
